newsitem.title: GREECE: New Bank/Greece deputy gov favours hard drachma.
newsitem.headline: New Bank/Greece deputy gov favours hard drachma.

text.p: Greece's new deputy central bank governor, Nikolaos Garganas, is known for his tough stance against inflation and his support for the hard drachma policy.
Garganas was sworn in on Thursday by President of the Republic Costis Stephanopoulos in a ceremony attended by Bank of Greece governor Lucas Papademos. He replaces Evangelos Kourakos.

An economist who studied at the London Scool of Economics, Garganas obtained his PhD from University College London. He worked as a research economist at Britain's National Institute for Economic and Social Research during 1968-1975.
Since 1975 he has been an advisor to the Bank of Greece and a founding member of the council of economic advisors.

Garganas was the mastermind of an economic stabilisation programme during a previous socialist administration in 1985-87. The programme was implemented by then national economy minister Costas Simitis, who is now the prime minister.

He has monitored European integration closely as a member of the EU monetary committee in 1985-87. He is also the author of three books and numerous papers on macroeconomic analysis, econometric models, international trade and monetary policy.

In December 1993 he returned to the EU monetary committee, made up of anti-inflation hawks. He places a top priority on fighting inflation and has been among the most ardent supporters of the Greek central bank's hard drachma policy. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
